samples.summary: New mandatory nonce on `?mode=cli` hard-breaks every already-installed CLI against an upgraded backend
samples.evidence: `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` now throws `BadRequestException('Missing or invalid CLI login nonce…')` for any `mode=cli` request lacking `nonce`. The CLI is a separately-installed npm package (`packages/cli`, `bin.ts`), so the moment the hosted backend ships this, every user running a previously-published `wafflebase` binary gets a 400 on `wafflebase login` and cannot authenticate at all until they upgrade — there is no grace/deprecation window. The design note (docs/design/cli.md:797) waves this away with "Backend and CLI ship from the same tree; upgrade the server first", which is true of the repo but not of installed clients. If a transition is wanted, the guard could accept a missing nonce (state.nonce undefined — the controller at auth.controller.ts:130 already handles that case) for a release before flipping to fail-closed.

samples.summary: `sawUnboundCallback` conflates a hostile/unrelated local request with an old server, letting any local process choose the login failure message and exit class
samples.evidence: Any request to `/callback?code=…` without a matching nonce sets `sawUnboundCallback = true` (line 300) — including the exact hostile-local-page case this binding exists to defeat, or a random port scanner. On timeout the CLI then reports `EXIT_SYSTEM_ERROR` with 'the server predates nonce-bound CLI login. Upgrade the server…' (lines 361-365), which is a wrong diagnosis (the server may be perfectly fine) and hands an attacker control over the exit class (2 instead of the user-error 1 that a plain timeout gets). Distinguishing 'nonce param absent entirely' (old server) from 'nonce present but mismatched' (injection) would at least narrow it, and even that is spoofable.

samples.summary: `classifyLoginFailure` omits `UserError`, so an `INVALID_URL` during login escapes as an unhandled rejection instead of the documented message/exit
samples.evidence: `classifyLoginFailure` only matches `LoginError | SystemError`. But `fetchOrThrow` (packages/cli/src/errors.ts:155) throws `UserError('INVALID_URL', …)` for an unparseable `--server`, and `fetchLoginSession` calls it three times. `wafflebase login --server 'not a url'` therefore returns `null` from `classifyLoginFailure`, the action rethrows (line 66), and since `bin.ts:27` uses `program.parse()` (not `parseAsync`) the rejection is unhandled — the user gets a raw stack trace rather than the documented one-line `Invalid URL "…". Check --server / WAFFLEBASE_SERVER.` (docs/design/cli.md:1041). The exit code happens to still be 1 only because Node's default unhandled-rejection exit is 1.
searchedFor: read packages/cli/src/bin.ts for parse vs parseAsync

samples.summary: Manual-redirect loop never consumes the 3xx response body, leaking the undici connection for each hop
samples.evidence: With `redirect: 'manual'` the redirect response still has a body. The loop reads only `res.headers.get('location')` and then `continue`s (lines 261-270) without `res.body?.cancel()` / `await res.text()`. undici does not release the socket back to the pool until the body is consumed or cancelled, so every redirected image hop holds a connection for the life of the export (up to 6 per image). The `!res.ok` branch at line 272 has the same issue for error bodies.

samples.summary: Redirect-loop failure is reported as `IMAGE_URL_BLOCKED` (user error), which the documented error matrix reserves for a `src` the CLI refuses to dereference
samples.evidence: `blocked('Image fetch failed: too many redirects for …')` yields code `IMAGE_URL_BLOCKED` and exit 1. Per docs/design/cli.md:1042 that code means 'Image `src` the CLI refuses to dereference'; a redirect loop is remote-server behaviour, so an agent branching on the code will misattribute it to a malformed document. Note the accompanying message is also inconsistent with the other `blocked()` messages, which all start with 'Refusing to fetch'.

samples.summary: `httpError(res.status, msg)` lets a server-supplied message override the documented AUTH_ERROR text on 401/403
samples.evidence: `throw httpError(res.status, msg)` passes the backend's `error.message` for every status. For 401/403 `httpError` (errors.ts:76-78) keeps code `AUTH_ERROR` but uses that message instead of the single-sourced `AUTH_FAILED_MESSAGE`, so the 'Authentication failed. Run `wafflebase login`.' line the error matrix (docs/design/cli.md:1038) promises does not appear on this path. Exit class is still correct (2).

samples.summary: `fetchLoginSession` parses three JSON bodies unguarded; a non-JSON 2xx (proxy/HTML) throws a SyntaxError that the new contract does not classify
samples.evidence: `await exchangeRes.json()` (112), `await meRes.json()` (130) and `await wsRes.json()` (145) are only reached on `res.ok`, but an ok-status non-JSON response (captive portal, misconfigured proxy) rejects with a `SyntaxError`, which `classifyLoginFailure` returns `null` for → rethrow → unhandled rejection with a stack trace, contradicting the section's claim that login 'reads the same table'. Also `tokens.accessToken` is used unchecked at line 119/225, so a 200 with `{}` produces `Bearer undefined` and then `decodeJwtExpiry(undefined)`.

finding.summary: New mandatory nonce on `?mode=cli` hard-breaks every already-installed CLI against an upgraded backend
finding.evidence: `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` now throws `BadRequestException('Missing or invalid CLI login nonce…')` for any `mode=cli` request lacking `nonce`. verdict.reason: The quoted code exists (github-auth.guard.ts:40-45 throws BadRequestException for mode=cli without a well-formed nonce), but it is not a correctness defect. The guard's condition contains no logic error: it matches the documented design (docs/design/cli.md:791-797) and fails closed with an actionable 400. The in-tree CLI always supplies a conforming nonce (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:171-175, a 43-char base64url string matching /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,128}$/), so no path in this repository breaks. The finding is purely about backward compatibility for previously-installed npm clients — a release/rollout policy tradeoff — and the remedy it proposes (temporarily accept a missing nonce) would reintroduce exactly the vulnerability the change closes (guard comment, github-auth.guard.ts:17-20: without the nonce the endpoint mints a login code and delivers it to an arbitrary 127.0.0.1:<port> with the CLI unable to distinguish it). That weighing of exposure vs. grace window belongs to the security and blast-radius lenses, which the Correctness lane explicitly defers. The symmetric case is also handled deliberately, not accidentally: a new CLI against an old server fails with a named cause rather than hanging (login.ts:358-364), confirming this is intentional version gating rather than a missing guard or inverted condition.
